note: Ground truth labelled by a Claude agent from the Muse Voice Transcribe narration and 1 fps frames, blind to the model's plan; not yet human-reviewed. Uncertain: the wire-to-terminal step is shown only as an arrow overlay (wires never seen pushed in), mounting the new thermostat face is never shown, and the narration's 'white yellow green red' does not match the visible blue/green/red/white wires.

steps.instruction: Pull the cover off the old Honeywell thermostat.
steps.done_looks_like: The old thermostat's mechanism and wiring base are exposed on the wall with the cover removed.
steps.evidence: Transcript [0.0] 'let's take off the old one'; frames t=6-7 hand pulls cover away, t=8 bare base on wall.

steps.instruction: Hold a voltage tester to the old thermostat wiring to check for power.
steps.done_looks_like: The tester tip sits at the thermostat terminals and lights up, showing the wires are live.
steps.evidence: Transcript [8.1] 'Let's check for the voltage', [10.4] 'there is low voltage'; frames t=9-11 yellow tester at terminals, flashes blue at t=11.

steps.instruction: Switch off the furnace breaker in the breaker box.
steps.done_looks_like: The furnace breaker in the panel is in the off position.
steps.evidence: Transcript [10.4] 'turn off the breaker... find the furnace'; t=15-18 panel only (no hands, so not the start), t=19 hand flips a breaker, t=20 tester near panel.

steps.instruction: Check the old thermostat wiring again with the voltage tester to confirm there is no power.
steps.done_looks_like: The tester touches each terminal and shows only its green ready light, no voltage alert.
steps.evidence: Transcript [21.0] 'check for the voltage one more time', [23.3] 'now we can proceed'; frames t=21-28 tester probes several terminals with green light only, t=29-30 tester gone.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the two screws and pull the old base plate off the wall.
steps.done_looks_like: The old base plate is held away from the wall, its wires still attached, with the wall hole visible.
steps.evidence: Transcript [23.3] 'two screws... let's just take them off', [32.1] take a picture of the wiring; t=31 drill on screw, t=32-38 hand holds the old base showing wires on W/Y/G/R. Merged the 'note the wiring' advice into this step because no photo-taking is shown; wire disconnection is not shown.

steps.instruction: Screw the new Honeywell base plate to the wall with the wires fed through its opening.
steps.done_looks_like: The white new base plate is screwed flat on the wall with the blue, green, red and white wires coming through above the terminal block.
steps.evidence: Transcript [32.1] 'Secure the plate to the wall'; t=39-41 screwdriver driving plate screws, t=42 plate mounted with both screws in.

steps.instruction: Connect each wire to the matching terminal on the new base: G, Y, W and R, the same letters it used on the old base.
steps.done_looks_like: Four wires are secured under the G, Y, W and R terminals of the new base; B, O and RC are empty.
steps.evidence: Transcript [41.7] 'connect the wire to the terminal... same terminal'; t=44-58 split screen of new base (labels B O G Y W NOT-USED R RC) beside old base (labels W, Y, G and a top-right R), red arrows at t=54-56 on the old terminals and t=57 under G, Y, W, R on the new. Hands never shown inserting wires and the finished wired state is never shown; terminal set read from the arrows.

steps.instruction: Switch the furnace breaker back on.
steps.done_looks_like: The furnace breaker is in the on position and the new thermostat display is lit.
steps.evidence: Transcript [58.8] 'turn the breaker on'; t=59 finger on breaker, t=60-61 new Honeywell Home thermostat mounted and showing 89. Mounting the thermostat face onto the base happens off-screen, so it is not its own step; t=62-65 furnace running has no hands.
